notes: BATCH A (paracetamol, co-codamol, codeine, tramadol, ibuprofen, naproxen). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). All quotes checked FOUND against the shared cache with lib/text.mjs quoteFound. NOT FOUND: (1) Paracetamol low body-weight / hepatic risk-factor maximum doses: none of the UK oral paracetamol SmPCs checked (Zentiva 9128 and 5164, Flamingo 13495/101491/101607, Ipca 12154, Panadol Original 6474, Panadol Advance 742, Calpol 6634, Rosemont 6694) state a reduced maximum dose; only SmPC 4.9 overdose risk factors (5 g with risk factors) are given, recorded as such. IV paracetamol SmPCs were not used (out of scope). (2) Codeine 30 mg SmPCs (Wockhardt 2375, Milpharm 7031) give no adult mg-per-dose for pain, only max 240 mg/day at intervals of at least 6 hours; the 30-60 mg dose is stated for ages 12-18. (3) No CrCl/eGFR threshold for tramadol in either tramadol SmPC used. (4) No SPS 'Suggestions for drug monitoring in adults in primary care' entry or monitoring page for paracetamol, codeine, co-codamol or tramadol was found; SPS 'NSAIDs monitoring' used for ibuprofen/naproxen. (5) Controlled-drug scheduling of codeine/tramadol is not stated in the sources used and is not claimed. (6) No UK source found requiring brand-name prescribing for any batch A medicine (brandPrescribing null). CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept as separate items/rules): (a) Paracetamol severe hepatic impairment: Rosemont 250mg/5ml SmPC lists severe hepatic dysfunction as a contraindication; Zentiva tablet and Calpol 120mg/5ml SmPCs only advise care. (b) Paracetamol post-vaccination fever at 2-4 months: current Calpol SmPC allows 2.5 ml up to 4 times a day; the older MHRA July 2011 DSU table says a second dose after 4-6 hours and no more than 2 doses. (c) Codeine breastfeeding: codeine SmPC 4.3 contraindicated vs 4.6 'not recommended'; MHRA 'should not be used'; SPS avoid. Rule uses contraindicated. (d) Codeine hepatic: SmPC 4.3 lists 'liver disease' and 'severe hepatic dysfunction' as contraindications while 4.4 says 'avoided or the dose reduced' in hepatic impairment; rule uses the 4.3 contraindication for any hepatic impairment - integrator may wish to review. (e) Tramadol pregnancy: both SmPCs 'should not be used in pregnant women' (avoid) vs BUMPS 'only if recommended by your doctor' and SPS 'reserve ... where other alternative analgesics have been ineffective' (caution). (f) Tramadol breastfeeding: capsule SmPC 'not recommended'; prolonged-release SmPC 'should not be used during lactation or ... breast-feeding should be discontinued'; SPS 'can be used short-term ... with caution and infant monitoring'. (g) Ibuprofen + methotrexate: Brufen tablets 'care should be taken' vs Pinewood suspension lists methotrexate under 'should be avoided in combination with'. (h) Ibuprofen NSAID-hypersensitivity and bleeding tendency: both SmPCs list these in section 4.3 (Brufen worded 'should not be used/given'); after audit both formulation-scoped rules are contraindicated. (i) Ibuprofen/naproxen breastfeeding: SmPCs 'avoid' vs SPS (ibuprofen NSAID of choice; naproxen short-term with caution). (j) Naproxen pregnancy: Naprosyn 500mg tablet SmPC 4.6 ends 'Naproxen is contraindicated during pregnancy' while its own 4.3 and the Naprosyn EC SmPC say last/third trimester only; rules follow 4.3 (T3 contraindicated, T1-T2 avoid unless clearly necessary) and the discrepancy is shown as a pregnancy item - please review. (k) Co-codamol 30/500 SmPC (Zentiva) lists opioid contraindications (acute asthma, respiratory depression, acute alcoholism, head injury, raised ICP, after biliary surgery, MAOIs) that the 8/500 SmPC (same MAH) does not; those rules are scoped to the 30/500 formulation. LEVEL POLICY (revised by independent audit 2026-10-17, see audit/A.md): anything listed in SmPC section 4.3 -> contraindicated, whatever the verb ('should not be used/given', 'use should be avoided'), per the audit brief ('contraindicated' = section 4.3 or 'must not'); this changed Brufen NSAID hypersensitivity/NERD and bleeding tendency, Naprosyn NSAID cross-sensitivity/NERD and codeine raised ICP/head injury from avoid to contraindicated. Sentences outside 4.3 worded 'should not be used/given' or 'avoid' -> avoid; 'not recommended' / 'not suitable' -> avoid; 'should only be treated after careful consideration and high doses should be avoided' (ibuprofen CV disease) -> dose. SCHEMA NOTES FOR INTEGRATOR: some condition rules also carry an 'age' bound (codeine/co-codamol/tramadol tonsillectomy-OSA and paediatric compromised breathing) - both should be required to match. Duplication rules use kind 'duplication' with 'other' (paracetamol <-> co-codamol). New conditions 'renal-impairment' and 'severe-renal-impairment' are used where the SmPC gives no eGFR/CrCl number (renal kind rules are used only where a CrCl threshold exists: naproxen CrCl < 30 ml/minute contraindicated). Paracetamol suspension 120 mg/5 ml age rule uses maxYears 0.1667 (2 months). GROUPS: memberships defined here with quotes: nsaid (ibuprofen, naproxen), opioid (codeine, co-codamol, tramadol), serotonergic (tramadol). Interaction rules also reference groups whose memberships must come from other batches: ssri, anticoagulant, antiplatelet, vitamin-k-antagonist, corticosteroid, ace-inhibitor, diuretic, antihypertensive, fluoroquinolone, sulfonamide, antacid, cyp3a4-inhibitor, cns-depressant. No master-list medicine was assigned to cns-depressant (the SmPCs name benzodiazepines, gabapentinoids, alcohol etc., none in the master list). SOURCES NOT USED / EXCLUDED: Calprofen 100mg/5ml SmPC (emc 339) - its age-band dosing table is garbled in the page text (bands and volumes not alignable), so the Pinewood 100mg/5ml SmPC (emc 4560) was used instead. MHRA DSU 'Codeine: very rare risk of side-effects in breastfed babies' (2007) not used because the 2013 MHRA advice (codeine should not be used when breastfeeding) supersedes it. SPS co-codamol supply-shortage page not used (time-limited supply information). COVERAGE: ibuprofen 200 mg and 600 mg tablets not separately covered (Brufen 400 mg SmPC used for prescription dosing). Tramadol prolonged-release capsules (e.g. Maxitram SR) not covered; Tilodol SR prolonged-release tablets used. AUDIT ADDENDUM 2026-10-17 (independent second check, details in audit/A.md): cross-direction interactions added on batch A side from other batches' SmPCs (warfarin emc-2803, spironolactone emc-1619, lisinopril emc-7611, metformin emc-987, methotrexate emc-10988 + SPS sps-mtx-interactions, sertraline emc-1070, clopidogrel emc-5935, ciprofloxacin emc-885, St John's wort THR mhra-thr-13668-0014). Naproxen renal rule 'CrCl >= 30 dose' (fired for normal renal function) replaced by a renal-impairment condition rule. New condition 'biliary-tract-surgery' (co-codamol 30/500 4.3). Codeine hepatic: 4.3 'liver disease' kept as contraindicated for any hepatic impairment after review. Naproxen pregnancy: 4.3 basis kept (T3 contraindicated, T1-T2 avoid) after review; Naprosyn 4.6 'contraindicated during pregnancy' wording still shown. Co-codamol 30/500 opioid contraindications remain scoped to 30/500 because the 8/500 SmPC does not list them. BACK-FILL 2026-10-17 (new master-list medicines and groups, from the batch A SmPCs already used): new interaction rules for metoclopramide/domperidone (paracetamol and co-codamol absorption speed; codeine opposes their GI effect), carbamazepine (paracetamol liver toxicity; tramadol reduced effect), tricyclic antidepressants (paracetamol 250mg/5ml SmPC only; co-codamol anticholinergic; codeine CNS depression; tramadol seizures), MAO inhibitors (co-codamol 30/500 contraindicated per its 4.3, 8/500 avoid per its 4.5; codeine avoid; tramadol contraindicated), antihistamines / sedating antihistamines, anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, SNRIs and mirtazapine (tramadol seizures), 5-HT3 antagonists, aspirin (ibuprofen, naproxen: avoid), ARBs, beta-blockers, sulfonylureas, fluconazole and CYP2C9 inhibitors, aminoglycosides. New memberships: cns-depressant (codeine, co-codamol, tramadol; replaces the earlier statement that no master-list medicine was assigned) and nephrotoxic (ibuprofen, naproxen). Not added: paracetamol to hepatotoxic (its SmPCs describe liver damage in overdose, not at therapeutic dose). Serotonin-syndrome rules for SNRIs, tricyclics and mirtazapine were not duplicated because those medicines are already in the serotonergic group used by tramadol:interaction:serotonergic. Benzodiazepine and MAOI groups currently have no master-list members (chlordiazepoxide-clidinium has no UK product, so its membership is not sourced here).
